At 129.00 the position is stopped by a 2.5% move in a name whose ordinary day is 5.15%, so holding does not actually express the bullish case — it buys the downside gap and sells the upside to noise.

thesis: This is an exit, not a new trade, and the reason is the stop rather than the price. The long was opened 2026-11-10 at 9.00 and is -7.1% at 8.36. Its stop sits at 8.09 — just 0.095, or 1.2%, above the 200-day low of 7.995 — in a name whose ATR14 is 0.3936, which is 4.71% of price. A stop a quarter of an ATR above a multi-year low is placed inside the level it is meant to shelter behind, so ordinary noise takes it out whether the thesis is right or not. Moving it to where it belongs, below 7.995 at say 7.60, makes risk 1.40 against 1.82 of reward to the 10.82 target: R:R 1.30 against a 2.0 swing floor. The position clears its floor only because the stop is in the wrong place, which per config/strategy.md means it failed the floor.
key_risk: Huntsman is a cyclical at -48% off its high, so it is exactly the kind of name that doubles off a washout — exiting at 8.36 may be selling the low. Thin liquidity cuts both ways: $23.5M average dollar volume means a limit order may not fill at 8.36 on a gap-down open, and chasing it lower costs more than the 3.2% this exit is trying to save.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding: the 8.09 stop is 2.31 ATR from the 9.00 entry, which clears the swing floor on the published arithmetic, and the trade has used only 0.64 of the 0.91 it was designed to risk — honouring a stop you set is the whole point of setting one, and closing early at 8.36 is the discretionary override that makes stops meaningless. Answered on the numbers rather than by assertion: a stop clears the ATR floor measured from entry and still be unusable measured against the chart, and this one is both. It is 0.69 ATR from the current 8.36 and 0.24 ATR above the 200-day low, so the distribution of outcomes between here and there is dominated by whether 7.995 gets probed, not by whether chemicals demand recovers. The exit is not an override of the stop; it is the recognition that this stop was never a risk control.
